sections.html:
Walterboro anchors Colleton County, a big, wet slice of the Lowcountry covering 1,133.28 square miles, 1,056.50 of them land. Three rivers, the Edisto, the Salkehatchie and the Ashepoo, cross it, and protected ground such as Bear Island and Donnelley takes up a fair share of the map.

The 2020 count was 38,604 residents, with an estimate of 39,382 for 2025. Population has held between about 38,000 and 39,000 since 2000, so houses here move in a calm market. Retail, health care and food service provide most jobs, and Colleton County School District, Cracker Barrel, Food Lion and Walmart are among the bigger employers.

Colleton splits tax work across three desks. The Assessor puts a value on property. The Auditor turns that value into a tax figure. The Treasurer takes the payment. Land and building records live with the Assessor, and personal property and vehicle records live with the Auditor, so an address correction must reach the right one.

  • Treasurer: 118 Benson Street, Tax Center Building, Walterboro, SC 29488. Phone 843-549-2233. Open Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with a drop box available around the clock.
  • Delinquent Tax Office: 118 Benson Street, P.O. Box 472. Phone 843-549-5433.
  • Assessor: 31 Klein Street, Harrelson Building, Room 309, Walterboro. Phone 843-549-1213.

Payment routes include the county's website, the state portal at ssl.sc.gov, the counter, the drop box, and a mailed check carrying your PIN so it posts to the correct account. Phone the Treasurer before choosing a method, since procedures shift.

Colleton follows S.C. Code 12-45-180 for late charges. Unpaid at January 16 (or 30 days after notices go out, whichever is later), a bill gains 3%. By February 2 it gains 7% more, and by March 17 another 5%.

If anything is still owed on March 17, the county treasurer hands an execution to the officer who collects delinquent tax. For mailed checks, the U.S. postmark is the test of timeliness.

The December 31 owner of record is the one named on the bill. A house that closes after December 31 leaves the next year's tax with the buyer. Ask the Treasurer for a billing and payoff figure so no stray balance surprises you at the table.

sections.h2: How a Colleton County tax sale works
sections.html:
Once a year, Colleton auctions parcels with unpaid tax. This year's auction is Friday, December 11, 2026, at the Colleton Civic Center, 494 Hampton St., Walterboro. Check-in opens at 9:00 a.m. and bidding starts at 10:00 a.m., running alphabetically by the taxpayer's surname.

The opening bid equals the delinquent tax for tax year 2025 and earlier plus the 2026 tax. Bidders who win and then fail to pay owe a $500 fine per bid. Title passes without warranty, and the sale leaves existing liens standing.

Redemption is allowed for 12 months under S.C. Code 12-51-90. The taxpayer in default, a grantee of the owner, and a mortgage or judgment creditor can all redeem, paying interest calculated on the bid.

Months after the saleInterest on the bid
1 to 33%
4 to 66%
7 to 99%
10 to 1212%

To learn the last redemption day for a particular parcel, phone the Delinquent Tax Office.

Reappraisal rolls through South Carolina counties on a staggered five-year plan. In Colleton, the Assessor owes you a notice whenever value or classification shifts by $1,000 or more. Market value can rise at most 15% inside one five-year cycle, but new construction, major additions and renovation are valued at the current market.

The 4% ratio goes to owner-occupied primary residences. All other property is assessed at 6%. You have to ask for the lower ratio, and you can file at any point before the first penalty date, January 15. Aim to file right after your deed or bond for title is recorded and you have moved in. Tell the Assessor about a change of use or owner within six months. A buyer cannot inherit your approval and must file anew.

  • Object in writing to the Assessor within 90 days of the date on the notice.
  • A field review follows, and the Assessor replies in writing.
  • Disagree with the reply? File a written appeal with the Colleton County Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days.
  • No notice that year? An appeal filed ahead of the first penalty date counts for the current year, and a later one counts for the next.

Unhappiness over a bigger bill is not an appeal ground by itself. Millage is set annually by the taxing bodies.

People aged 65 or older, people who are totally and permanently disabled, and legally blind owners may qualify to exclude the first $50,000 of the fair market value of a legal residence. Surviving spouses may qualify as well. The Auditor's Office has the requirements and the form.

sections.h2: Selling a Colleton County house with unpaid tax
sections.html:
Back taxes will not stop a closing. The title company normally settles them out of the seller's proceeds. Insist on a payoff in writing from the Treasurer or the Delinquent Tax Office, because penalty steps and the year-end auction both move the total.

  1. Request that written payoff with a date near your planned closing.
  2. Confirm the 4% application sits on file under the correct owner, especially for a vacant, rented or inherited house, since no application means 6%.
  3. Give the Assessor and the Auditor your present mailing address.
  4. If your parcel is on the auction list, either pay before the sale or build the redemption window into your plans.

A cash sale avoids the repairs and showings of a normal listing, which helps when a tax date is close.

Before you list, collect the dated assessment notice, last year's tax bill with its PIN, and a note of when the deed or bond for title was recorded. Those three items answer most of what a buyer's lender or the Assessor will ask. If the property was vacant, rented or inherited at any point, tell the title company early so any rate question is settled before the payoff is ordered. The Treasurer, the Delinquent Tax Office and the Assessor are all in Walterboro, and each one answers its own part of the bill. Early calls to the Auditor and Assessor take little time and can head off a delay at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Colleton County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer's Office, 118 Benson Street in Walterboro, in the drop box, through the county website or ssl.sc.gov, or by check with your PIN written on it. The phone is 843-549-2233.

faqs.q: When is the 2026 Colleton County tax sale?
faqs.a: Friday, December 11, 2026, at the Colleton Civic Center, 494 Hampton St., Walterboro. Registration starts at 9:00 a.m. and bidding begins at 10:00 a.m.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem property after a Colleton tax sale?
faqs.a: Twelve months under state law, with interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% depending on the quarter. Phone the Delinquent Tax Office to confirm the final day for your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I get the 4% rate on my Colleton County home?
faqs.a: Submit a legal residence application to the Assessor before January 15. Owner-occupied primary homes qualify, and any change in use must be reported within six months.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Colleton County assessment?
faqs.a: Mail the Assessor a written objection within 90 days of the dated notice. If the result stands, take it to the Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days of the written findings.
